$comment: The takeoff review visual law. ONE declaration, two consumers: apps/web/src/runs/palette.ts (the /runs screen and its PNG export) and eval/rhvac/render-zone-promotion.py (the offline agent-review renderer). Neither may hold a colour or a layer rule the other cannot see. Before this file existed the two surfaces had already diverged: /runs deleted the invented-closure dither at feedback round 2 ('read as confusion, not honesty') and the python renderer kept drawing it, so the human and the delegated eyes were judging different claims.
laws: The VERDICT render draws only what the solver claims exists, over what is actually there. Nothing invented. No input layer except the zone outline.
Decisions, evidence, and inputs never share a hue family.
Status is never carried by the candidate boundary. The candidate fill edge IS the boundary.
Received ink is the only near-opaque neutral. Invented closure is a translucent warm tint, never dithered, never screened.
The plan is what is there. The ink raster is what the solver saw. Judge against what is there; adjudicate against what it saw.

plan.$comment: 6000px Revit export with an exact affine (topLeft/topRight/bottomLeft in model feet). The export is halftone-light: measured, 1.44% of pixels sit at or below 185 and that band is the whole linework. Stretch it.

ink.$comment: replay seed ink, 0.5ft cells. EVIDENCE, not substrate. Forensic render only.

fill.$amendment: v1.1 2026-08-23. v1 said 'saturated' and 'fillDarkened' without numbers, so each consumer would have invented its own and the two surfaces would have drifted on day one. These are the values lane W shipped; they are now the law.
fill.$comment: Saturated translucent, stable across runs so an A/B keeps its colours. Adjacent candidates must differ enough that the seam between two fills reads as a boundary at 1px.

zone.$comment: kaitpw ruling 2026-08-23: zone authority stays visible in the verdict render, but hairline. It is an input, not a result, and it may never be the heaviest stroke in the image.

invented.$comment: Sealers manufacture obstruction. Forensic render only, translucent warm tint, never dithered.

$washAmendment: v1.2 2026-08-23. v1 was WRONG: voidWash and excludedWash both composited to RGB 226 over white and were indistinguishable (found by lane R implementing them faithfully). Worse, kaitpw's first annotation pass flagged excluded residue in 4 of 4 zones - it is the top-ranked defect class - so it must be the more legible of the two, never a near-invisible wash. Void stays a neutral grey; excluded becomes a warm tint that a 1 ft sliver still shows.

label.$comment: Status letter + candidate id. Small, on the fill, never on the boundary.
